name: SuperDoc
kind: Document engine for DOCX, built directly on OOXML
leads: Highest round-trip fidelity in the trial
detail: 100% on the corpus: 31 of 31 critical features, every word of text, all 35 package parts, and a genuine re-save that passes untouched parts through byte for byte. Report C calls its own UI the closest thing to a Word clone.
renderSection: 2.1 SuperDoc — the closest thing to a Word clone

name: Folio
kind: Browser editor and framework-neutral OOXML engine
leads: 98.5% fidelity with every word and every part kept
detail: 100% text retention and all 35 parts survive; the only loss is the w14 paragraph ids. Folio's compareDocx is one of only two document-comparison implementations found in source across the twelve projects.

name: GenOffice
kind: Open-source AI Office suite: Docs, Sheets, Slides and PDF
leads: 98.5% fidelity, and the only editor that labels the SmartArt band
detail: All 35 parts kept with one block regenerated. In Report C it is the one editor that labels the SmartArt band, and its compareDocuments is the other comparison implementation found in source. The whole DOCX path is in the Apache-2.0 tree.
renderSection: 2.3 GenOffice — the only editor that labels the SmartArt band

name: eigenpal
license: Apache-2.0 (Pro packages under the EigenPal Pro License)
kind: Document engine with React and Vue adapters and an Office.js-style Editor API
leads: A near-exact reproduction of Word's page 3
detail: 98.5% on features with every package part kept. The main report ranks its DOM-free layout engine second for depth, and Report C finds its page 3 a near-exact match for Word's.

name: office-open
kind: Typed generator and parser for Word, Excel, PowerPoint, RTF and OpenDocument
leads: Every word of text kept, at 95.5% fidelity
detail: 100% text retention and all 35 parts present after the round trip, from a library that generates, parses and patches Office documents from JSON or typed APIs with no Office installed. It is also the engine under Docen.
renderSection: 2.6 Office-Open — a library, not an editor

name: Docen
kind: Editor on TipTap, ProseMirror and LeaferJS that paginates by Word's stacking rules
leads: Word's page count, on its own pagination
detail: 92.0% fidelity with 99.4% of the text and all 35 parts kept. Report C finds it lands on Word's page count; its README says its pagination follows Word's document grid, repeated table headers and float wrapping.
renderSection: 2.5 Docen — right page count, wrong chart

name: WordCraft
kind: Native word processor in Rust, with its own layout engine
leads: The deepest page-layout engine in the trial
detail: Report C: its own renderer, and it is very good. It keeps the chart, all four SmartArt parts, the OLE object, the embedded workbook and the image, and it has the widest in-process conversion set of the twelve.
renderSection: 2.7 WordCraft — its own renderer, and it is very good

name: Fidus Writer
kind: Academic writing tool; the measured tree is its schema, importer and exporter
leads: Highest hostile-input grade in the trial
detail: 0.72 in Report D: a ceiling on deep nesting and seven of the ten hostile packages cleaned, tied with LibreOffice for the most. It exports to JATS, HTML, LaTeX, Pandoc JSON, EPUB, DOCX and ODT.
renderSection: 2.11 Fidus Writer — the text renders, the table does not exist

name: Plate.js
kind: Plugin framework for rich-text editors, with a headless DOCX import and export
leads: The best behaviour on malformed input in the trial
detail: Its diagnostic vocabulary and its lossPolicy: 'reject' default are the best handling of malformed input measured, and it grades 0.70 on hostile packages, with named ceilings on decompression, entry flood and deep nesting.

name: docs.plus
kind: Real-time collaborative editor with a chatroom on every heading
leads: Six of ten hostile packages cleaned
detail: 0.60 in Report D: decompression, entry flood, attributes, zip-slip, external relationships and active content all come out clean, and 91.7% of the text survives the round trip.
renderSection: 2.10 docs.plus — the corpus arrives as HTML

name: canvas-editor
kind: Canvas and SVG editor that owns its whole rendering pipeline
leads: Cleaned the entity, zip-slip and active-content packages
detail: Six of the ten hostile packages come out clean in Report D, including the entity package, which most editors refuse and one keeps. Typography does not depend on the browser's editing host.
renderSection: 2.8 Canvas-Editor — the body does not render

name: Docxodus
kind: Structure-aware OOXML engine for .NET, WebAssembly, npm and Python
leads: Word's page geometry, to the pixel
detail: Report C: its rasterised page geometry is identical to Word's own export and it paginates into the same 6 pages. Its round trip is the best in the study: 100.0% on the 97 checks with 35 of 35 parts kept, none changed and none dropped, and it is the only editor that keeps the w15, w16cid, w16du and w10 namespaces.
renderSection: 2.13 Docxodus — the engine that draws what it cannot render

name: LibreOffice
kind: The baseline: a full office suite, converted headlessly
leads: The only renderer that matches Word's pagination and every piece of page furniture
detail: Report C: exactly 6 pages, the header, the page number and the footer all where Word puts them. On the round trip it is the calibration floor at 86.0%, not a candidate.
